designation: IN THE COURT OF DISTRICT & SESSIONS JUDGE
jurisdictionNote: District-level criminal and civil courts in Meghalaya, supervised by the High Court of Meghalaya (principal seat at Shillong). Following the 2021 reorganisation, Meghalaya has 12 districts. English is the working language; Khasi and Garo are recognised regional languages under the Meghalaya State Language Act, 2005. Sixth Schedule autonomous district councils (Khasi Hills, Jaintia Hills, Garo Hills) operate parallel customary courts.

party_designation.state: State of Meghalaya through the Principal Secretary, Home Department, Government of Meghalaya, Shillong

prayer_language.closing: And for this act of kindness, the petitioner shall, as in duty bound, ever pray.

verification_format:
I, {deponent_name}, {designation}, do hereby solemnly verify and declare that the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ of the above petition are true to my personal knowledge and the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ are based on information received and legal advice tendered, which I believe to be true. Nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

DEPONENT
localRules: English is the language of pleadings before the subordinate judiciary in Meghalaya; Khasi and Garo pleadings with English translation may be accepted at the discretion of the court.
Bail applications under S.483 BNSS (formerly S.439 CrPC) before the Sessions Court must disclose any prior rejection and be accompanied by a certified copy of the FIR.
Anticipatory bail applications (S.482 BNSS) require certified copy of the FIR and grounds of apprehension; the High Court of Meghalaya is the preferred forum for serious offences.
Vakalatnama in the form prescribed under the High Court of Meghalaya Rules with requisite court-fee stamp.
Court-fee under the Court-Fees Act, 1870 as adopted by Meghalaya with State amendments.
SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, POCSO and NDPS cases tried by designated Special Courts at the district headquarters.

Sixth Schedule autonomous district councils — Khasi Hills, Jaintia Hills, Garo Hills — operate parallel customary courts (Village/Subordinate District Council Courts) under the United Khasi-Jaintia Hills Autonomous District (Administration of Justice) Rules, 1953 and Garo Hills Autonomous District (Administration of Justice) Rules, 1954. Advocate must verify forum jurisdiction (autonomous council court vs. regular sessions/district court) before filing — particularly for matters involving tribal customary law, land, inheritance and personal law.
e_filing_note: e-Filing operational at Shillong, Tura via eCourts portal; not yet mandatory state-wide.
